newsitem.title: USA: Dole warns voters to read Clinton fine print.
newsitem.headline: Dole warns voters to read Clinton fine print.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole warned voters to read the "fine print" in President Bill Clinton's campaign promises, calling the election a contest between Clinton's "warmed-over liberal ideas" and his own "common-sense conservative" ones.

In the text of his weekly radio address, to air on Saturday morning -- just a day before the first presidential debate in Hartford, Connecticut, on Sunday -- Dole said there were real differences in the two candidates' visions for America.

"It really boils down to a contest between the warmed-over liberal ideas of President Clinton and my common-sense conservative ideas that put the opportunities, safety and future of our children and families before government," Dole said, according to a text of the address.
He also continued to hammer away at the trust issue, telling Americans Clinton would say he supported many of the same positions as Dole on education, taxes, violent crime and drugs.

"But, listen carefully. If it were a contract, you'd need to read the fine print," Dole said. "The president will talk about tax cuts, but don't forget the last time he promised them we wound up with the largest tax increase in history."
He said Clinton would promise to help families, but "thanks in large part to him the average family now pays more in taxes than for food, shelter and clothing combined."

Dole also blasted Clinton for opposing vouchers to allow parents to send their children to private schools, his appointment of "countless liberal judges," and moves to eliminate drug enforcement agency officers.
"Our differences are really quite simple," Dole said. "President Clinton sees higher taxes and bigger government as the answer to our problems. I see high taxes and big government as the problem."
